premiseMatrix.evidence: Direct provider prose calls the payload an LZMA stream and explicitly says it is not the .xz container format.
The documented daily BI5 Python decoder reads compressed bytes and calls lzma.decompress(compressed) without format or filters.
The official function signature gives lzma.decompress(data, format=FORMAT_AUTO, memlimit=None, filters=None).
FORMAT_AUTO detects the container and decompresses .xz and .lzma files.
Python defines FORMAT_ALONE as the legacy .lzma container and says FORMAT_AUTO decompresses .lzma files.
Python states data in FORMAT_RAW cannot be decompressed using FORMAT_AUTO.
Python requires a custom filter chain when the raw format is used for decompression.
Python names FORMAT_ALONE as the legacy .lzma container format.

terminologyDistinction.naturalLanguage: Dukascopy's natural-language raw LZMA wording means LZMA bytes outside the XZ container in this adjudication record.
terminologyDistinction.pythonApi: Python FORMAT_RAW is a separate API format requiring an explicit filter chain and is not inferred from the natural-language phrase.

candidateFormats.reason: Direct Dukascopy wording excludes the .xz container.
After direct exclusion of XZ and documented incompatibility of RAW with the sample's default call, legacy .lzma is the only FORMAT_AUTO-compatible format remaining.
FORMAT_RAW requires a filter chain and cannot be decoded by the documented default FORMAT_AUTO call; no source supplies a filter chain.

uniqueConclusionReason: FORMAT_ALONE remains the only frozen operational candidate under the current cross-source reconciliation, but provider intent is not directly source-specified.
